title: Unlink a node_modules junction before deleting the tree that holds it
body:
Unlink the junction first (fs.unlink on the link path, which Node reports as a symbolic link), then delete the tree. Never run git worktree remove --force on a worktree whose node_modules is a junction to the main checkout. If the main node_modules was emptied anyway, restore it with npm ci from npm-shrinkwrap.json; the embedding model lives in the data directory, not node_modules, so it survives.

Why: On 2026-10-07 git worktree remove --force followed the node_modules junction and emptied the main checkout's node_modules (0 entries left). Node's fs.unlink on the junction followed by fs.rm recursive on the parent kept the target intact in a scratch test, and src/eval/agent/run.js now unlinks its junction before removing each clone.

evidence.summary: unlinks the shared node_modules junction before rm of the clone, with a comment naming git worktree remove --force as the cause
model cacheDir is join(resolveDataBase(), 'models'), outside node_modules

v1.trigger: When removing a git worktree or a scratch clone on Windows that links the repository's node_modules through a junction
